lines.trans: Look at the left side of the watercolour sketch—there is a tiny carved leaf!
Walk around the dry side of the basin, Nour; do you see it on the stone?
Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
Are you sure about this narrow lane, Rami? My compass says that bends south.
I have lived on Jasmine Street for twenty years, Tariq, and alleys beat compasses!
Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Rami?
Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighbourhood lane?
All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: I will certainly come to the party.

examples.text: أكيد ما رح أنسى أجبلك الكتاب بكرة الصبح.
examples.trans: For sure I won't forget to bring you the book tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: أنا وإياك رح نخلص المشروع قبل يوم الخميس.
examples.trans: You and I will finish the project before Thursday.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Form VIII verb; frequently used in imperatives for following directions or clues.

examples.text: اتبعوا الخريطة خطوة بخطوة عشان ما تضيعوا.
examples.trans: Follow the map step by step so you do not get lost.

examples.text: دايما بنتبع البوصلة لما نمشي بالزقاق.
examples.trans: We always follow the compass when we walk through the alley.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحتاج, بيحتاج).

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.
An old house needs steady care.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بختار, بيختار).

examples.trans: I chose this quarter for a family reason.
They chose a table under the tree.

meanings.note: Used in everyday speech for a shorter route as well as a shortened word.

examples.text: رامي دايما بلاقي اختصار سريع من ورا الساحة.
examples.trans: Rami always finds a quick shortcut behind the courtyard.

examples.text: بلاش نجرب أي اختصار واحنا مستعجلين.
examples.trans: Let us not try any shortcut while we are in a hurry.

meanings.note: Construct form of اطنعش used directly before a singular noun.

examples.text: دقت الساعة اطنعشر دقة وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The clock struck twelve chimes at noon.

examples.text: في اطنعشر كرسي حوالين طاولة الساحة.
examples.trans: There are twelve chairs around the courtyard table.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical tower, a skyscraper, or an astrological sign.

examples.trans: This is the highest tower in the city.

examples.text: برج الساعة القديم مبين من فوق السطوح.
examples.trans: The old clock tower is visible from the rooftop.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Loanword used for urban street blocks as well as building bricks.

examples.text: المكتبة بعيدة تلات بلوكات لفوق بالشارع.
examples.trans: The library is three blocks up the street.

examples.text: بنينا الحيط الصغير من حجر البلوك.
examples.trans: We built the low wall out of concrete blocks.

meanings.note: Used for navigation or metaphorically for direction.

examples.text: ضاع بالصحراء لأنه ما كان معه بوصلة.
examples.trans: He got lost in the desert because he didn't have a compass.

examples.text: اتبعنا إبرة البوصلة لحد ما وصلنا الشرق.
examples.trans: We followed the compass needle until we reached the east.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: لقينا البطاقة التانية تحت الصحن الأبيض.
examples.trans: We found the second card under the white plate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: The number 3 when followed by a counted noun.

examples.trans: I have three cars in the garage.

examples.text: مشينا تلات دقايق وبعدين وصلنا عالبوابة.
examples.trans: We walked three minutes and then reached the gate.

meanings.note: Small hill (plural تلال tilaal); familiar across hilly Amman.

examples.text: عمان مبنية على تلال حلوة بتطل عالسما.
examples.trans: Amman is built across lovely hills looking out at the sky.

examples.text: لما نقسم الشغل الكبير لتلال صغيرة بصير سهل.
examples.trans: When we break a big job into small hills, it becomes easy.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize absolute completion or exactness.

examples.trans: I agree with you completely.

examples.text: النتيجة طلعت متل ما توقعنا تماما.
examples.trans: The result turned out exactly as we expected.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guests arrived from the south in the morning.
The weather is warm in the south today.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: We found a strange stone in the garden.

examples.text: لقينا حجر منحوت عليه نجمة صغيرة.
examples.trans: We found a stone with a small star carved on it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for later.
That is kind, honest talk.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; covers expeditions, cleaning drives, and campaigns.

examples.text: قود الحملة يا كابتن واحنا وراك بالخريطة.
examples.trans: Lead the expedition, captain, and we are right behind you with the map.

examples.text: الحارة عملت حملة تنظيف للساحة يوم السبت.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood organized a cleanup campaign for the square on Saturday.

meanings.note: Spatial and approximate preposition.

examples.text: امشي حوالي الجهة الناشفة من النافورة.
examples.trans: Walk around the dry side of the fountain.

examples.text: في حوالي عشرين كتاب قديم عالرف.
examples.trans: There are around twenty old books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural أحواض. Used for courtyard fountain basins, flowerbeds, and sinks.

examples.trans: The paper landed in the middle of the fountain basin.
There is a planter basin of green mint in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: In Jordanian urban speech, دخلة specifically means a narrow lane or turn-off.

examples.text: هاي الدخلة الضيقة بتوصل دغري عالساحة.
examples.trans: This narrow lane leads straight to the courtyard.
The entrance lane to the house is lined with jasmine trees.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Covers daqqa ('a knock / clock chime', pl. دقات) and diqqa ('precision / punctuality', الدقة بالمواعيد).

examples.text: سمعنا اطنعشر دقة من برج الساعة.
examples.trans: We heard twelve chimes from the clock tower.
I always love punctuality.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رئيسية, plural: رئيسيين).

examples.trans: We shut off the main water valve in the cellar.
The main gate is on the quiet street.

meanings.note: Active participle of راح ('to go'), used like a present progressive in Levantine ('am/is/are going').

examples.text: أنا وسلمى رايحين عالسوق نجيب ليمون.
examples.trans: Salma and I are heading to the market to get lemons.

examples.text: وين رايح بهالسلة الكبيرة يا زياد؟
examples.trans: Where are you heading with that big basket, Ziad?

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: A noun referring to a single drawing, illustration, or painting.

examples.trans: This drawing is very beautiful.

examples.text: في رسمة صغيرة لورقة زيزفون على الهامش.
examples.trans: There is a small drawing of a linden leaf in the margin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برمي, بيرمي).

examples.trans: Maybe he tossed my card in the bin.
Do not throw away the old receipt.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ساكنة, plural: ساكنين).

examples.trans: Does your older brother live here in Amman?
We used to live on Jasmine Street years ago.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: This car is this year's model.

examples.text: مرّت سنة كاملة على آخر زيارة للمزرعة.
examples.trans: A whole year has passed since the last visit to the farm.

meanings.note: Denotes a perimeter wall or stone garden wall around a yard or compound rather than an interior room wall (حيط).

examples.trans: The garden wall is covered with white jasmine.

examples.text: نط القط فوق سور الساحة وهرب.
examples.trans: The cat jumped over the courtyard wall and ran off.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Active participle of شاف ('to see'), standard in Jordanian for 'I see / do you see?'.

examples.text: شايفة رسمة المفتاح الدهبي فوق الباب!
examples.trans: I see the painted golden key above the door!
Do you see the yellow light in the attic window?

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ضيقة, plural: ضيقين).

examples.trans: The attic stairs are a bit narrow.
Do not enter the narrow alley.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Geminate verb (بعد / عدّيت) from root ع-د-د. Takes -ey- before consonant-initial past suffixes.

examples.trans: I can count them quickly.
I counted the envelopes twice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: المخبز بشتغل بنفس الوصفة من عشرين سنة.
examples.trans: The bakery has been using the same recipe for twenty years.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective formed from غرب (west); feminine غربية.

examples.text: القاعة الغربية فيها شبابيك كبيرة ومشمسة.
examples.trans: The western hall has big sunny windows.

examples.text: زرعنا النعناع بالركن الغربي من الحديقة.
examples.trans: We planted mint in the western corner of the garden.

غلب.gloss: to defeat; to beat; to overcome

meanings.en: to defeat; to beat; to overcome
meanings.note: Form I sound verb meaning to win against or surpass; in Form II غلّب means to trouble or bother someone.

examples.text: كيكة اللوز دايما بتغلب أي حلو تاني بالتذوق.
examples.trans: The almond cake always beats every other dessert at the tasting.

examples.text: مازن غلب أخوه بلعبة الألغاز مرتين.
examples.trans: Mazen beat his brother at the puzzle game twice.

meanings.note: Used to describe an empty container or a person who has free time.

examples.trans: I am free today in the afternoon.

examples.text: الرف الفوقاني فاضي، بنقدر نحط العلبة عليه.
examples.trans: The top shelf is empty; we can put the tin on it.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

قاد.gloss: to lead; to guide; to drive

meanings.en: to lead; to guide; to drive
meanings.note: Form I hollow verb (medial -w-); imperfect يقود / بقود. Used for leading people, teams, or clues leading somewhere.

examples.text: كل دليل قادنا للغرفة اللي ورا المكتبة.
examples.trans: Every clue led us to the room behind the library.

examples.text: سلمى قادت الفريق بحل اللغز بسرعة.
examples.trans: Salma led the team in solving the puzzle quickly.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Levantine word (qawwaar, plural qawaawiir) for a clay courtyard plant pot.

examples.text: زرعنا نعنع أخضر بقواوير فخار بالساحة.
examples.trans: We planted green mint in clay pots in the courtyard.

examples.text: سقت نور قوار الليمون جنب الدرج.
examples.trans: Nour watered the lemon pot beside the stairs.

meanings.note: Loanword used for ship/flight captains, sports team captains, and respectfully when addressing a male driver or waiter.

examples.text: الكابتن وجه الفريق كله بهدوء وثقة.
examples.trans: The captain guided the whole team calmly and confidently.

examples.text: صورة كابتن السفينة معلقة بمدخل القاعة.
examples.trans: The portrait of the ship's captain hangs at the hall entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.trans: I want tea, and also coffee.

examples.text: ذقنا التانية وكمان التالتة عشان نقارن القوام.
examples.trans: We tasted the second one and also the third to compare the texture.

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I will wait until you come.

examples.text: استنينا بالساحة لحد ما دقت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: We waited in the courtyard until the clock struck eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Used in Jordan to mean a wrap or a sandwich (e.g. falafel or shawarma), or a turn in the road.

examples.trans: I want a falafel sandwich with fries.

examples.text: أخذنا لفة سريعة بالسوق واشترينا زعتر وفستق.
examples.trans: We took a quick stroll around the market and bought thyme and pistachios.

meanings.note: Compound directional adverb combining لـ (toward) and فوق (above); opposite of لتحت.

examples.text: اطلع لفوق عالطابق التاني بتلاقي الغرفة.
examples.trans: Go upstairs to the second floor and you will find the room.
The red arrow on the map points upwards.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Compound Levantine interrogative (لـ 'to' + وين 'where').

examples.text: لوين نوجه المروحة عشان ينشف اللوح أسرع؟
examples.trans: Where should we point the fan so the panel dries faster?
Where are you heading in this rain without an umbrella?

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Relates to water, used for colors (light blue/watery), animals, or parks (e.g. water park).

examples.trans: We went to an aquatic amusement park (water park).

examples.text: استعمل الرسام لون مائي أزرق عشان يرسم البحر.
examples.trans: The painter used a blue watercolour to paint the sea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متأكدة, plural: متأكدين).

examples.trans: Are you sure you do not need this sweater?
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I went to Petra one time.

examples.text: جربنا الوصفة مرة تانية بس بخففنا السكر شوي.
examples.trans: We tried the recipe one more time, though we reduced the sugar slightly.

meanings.note: Form X active participle from root ق-و-م ('to stand straight'), describing lines, posture, or directions.

examples.trans: Walk straight down the street.
We drew a straight line with the ruler.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Noun of place from صبّ (to pour); designates the pouring spout of a jug or kettle as well as a river mouth.

examples.text: مصب إبريق الشاي النحاسي مزخرف بنقش ناعم.
examples.trans: The spout of the copper teapot is decorated with fine engraving.

examples.text: تجمع المي عند مصب النافورة بالحوش.
examples.trans: The water gathers at the fountain outlet in the yard.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Passive participle of نحت (to carve stone or wood); used for architectural reliefs and carved wooden items.

examples.text: في رقم منحوت على الحجر فوق البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a number carved into the stone above the gate.

examples.text: القوس المنحوت بالحيط قديم ومتقن كتير.
examples.trans: The carved arch in the wall is old and very finely crafted.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: مين كتب هاي الملاحظة عالورقة بالحبر الأزرق؟
examples.trans: Who wrote this note on the paper in blue ink?

meanings.note: Form II verb ميّز means 'to distinguish' or 'tell apart'.

examples.text: ما قدرت أميّز بين المرتبانين بدون ما أدوقهم.
examples.trans: I couldn't tell the two jars apart without tasting them.

examples.text: من بعيد ما بتميّز الخط إذا كان صغير كتير.
examples.trans: From far away you can't make out the writing if it's very small.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: The bread is dry, it can't be eaten.

examples.text: لازم نمسح الصحن بمنديل ناشف قبل ما نحط الكيكة.
examples.trans: We must wipe the plate with a dry cloth before putting the cake on.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Put the things here, please.

examples.text: الجو هون بالجبل أبرد بكثير من وسط البلد.
examples.trans: The weather up here on the hill is much cooler than downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian collective masculine noun for roses/flowers. Singular unit: وردة.

examples.trans: We walked past the flower stall.
The scent of roses and jasmine filled the courtyard.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Direction noun synonymous with شمال (left) in urban speech; frequently used as عاليسار (on the left).

examples.text: المكتبة موجودة على جهة اليسار بعد القوس.
examples.trans: The library is on the left side right after the arch.

examples.text: لفوا يسار عند النافورة بتلاقوا الممر.
examples.trans: Turn left at the fountain and you will find the passage.
